title: A private-image threat
scenario: Someone you met online says they have a private or embarrassing image of you and threatens to send it to classmates unless you pay or send more images. They tell you not to tell anyone.

answers.A: Pay once to buy time and keep the image from spreading while you decide what to do.
answers.B: Do not pay or send more; save evidence and tell a parent, guardian, counselor, or other trusted adult immediately, and use the platform’s reporting tools.
answers.C: Block the account after saving evidence and ask a trusted adult to help with reporting and account security.

explanation: Paying or sending more usually gives the person more leverage. Getting a trusted adult involved breaks the secrecy they depend on.
proTip: Secrecy protects the scammer, not you.
